summary.headline: CAMS Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record with non-MF revenue up ~24.5% YoY and EBITDA margin back at ~46.5%, while MF revenue was flat (+0.5% QoQ).
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and absolute EBITDA of about INR183 crores, with margin recovering to about 46.5% from 45% a year earlier. Non-MF revenue grew about 24.5% YoY and now contributes about 15.3% of enterprise revenue, with non-MF EBITDA margin above 16%. MF revenue was nearly flat, with AUM at INR55.1 lakh crores (down from INR58.5 lakh crores at one point in Q4 on Middle East-related market weakness) but up 21% YoY. Management guided to sub-5% employee cost growth and sub-9% total expense growth in FY27, flat KRA revenue, and at least 20% non-MF growth.

segments.name: Mutual fund (RTA/core)
segments.commentary: Revenue almost flat (~+0.5% YoY); AUM INR55.1 lakh crore, up 21% YoY with 68% overall share; yields stable, QoQ compression under 1% attributed to passive mix shift. Headcount in core MF operations reduced by ~70 YoY.

segments.name: Non-MF (overall)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~24.5% YoY, broad-based across CAMSPay, AIF, KRA; FY26 non-MF growth ~18% due to weak Q1. Non-MF EBITDA margin upwards of 16%, targeting 20% by end FY27.

segments.name: CAMSPay (payments)
segments.commentary: Payment aggregator (PA) and payment gateway (PG) both grew ~23% YoY; cards business ~25% of quarterly revenue, all non-MF; non-MF now above 50% of CAMSPay revenue.

segments.name: KRA
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% YoY despite demat/broking slowdown; NSE KRA integration added ~13-14 lakh PANs. Industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 expected to reduce revenue by INR8 crore, offset by INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift; management guides flat FY27 revenue.

segments.name: Alternatives (AIF)
segments.commentary: Revenue +25% YoY; AUM crossed INR3 lakh crore; 44 new full-service mandates incl. 14 new logos; 50% share of outsourced market.

segments.name: Repository / Insurance and others
segments.commentary: Rep revenue +6% YoY. Bima Central active users doubled; LIC started demat-format policy issuance. IR market share expanded to 40%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 employee cost growth guided below 5%; total expense growth guided below 9%, with a stated aim to be lower; increments effective from Q2 FY27.

Management aims to retain Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin (~46.5%) through FY27 after absorbing salary increases, investments and yield compression; no formal margin range given (bad quarter below 45%, good quarter ~46-47%).
Non-MF revenue growth of at least 20% in FY27 (~INR45-50 crore incremental on a ~INR250 crore base), with payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore.
KRA revenue guided flat in FY27 after ~INR8 crore price-cut impact offset by ~INR3 crore NSE KRA uplift and new-logo growth.
MF yield decline expected to be less than 3% (historical 3-3.5%); target 20% non-MF EBITDA margin by end of next year.
Revenue expected to grow on flat-to-falling headcount in FY27; ReArch expected to be a 5-year program, about 2 years done, ~3-4% behind schedule curve.
capex_capacity: ReArch cloud-native platform: 9 significant modules; transaction origination module fully built and launching to several thousand integrators; data lake (on Google Cloud BigQuery) to go live in 1H FY27; data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform ready within 3-4 months.
Team of close to 200 engineers on ReArch; headcount at FY26 end 8,420 vs 8,324 at FY25 end (ReArch hires >100; core MF headcount reduced ~70).
Form data extraction now runs in production with maker step removed (AI performs data entry; physical checker retained), ~1 million physical forms per month.
SIFs: 6 live as of Q4 FY26 after 4 launches in the quarter; ~8 more licensed or announced, with launches expected May-August 2026.

ConsenPro (DPDP compliance product, built in Think360) launched commercially; ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies expected to need it over 1.5 years. Unified device product (payments and KYC) noted as an adjacency.
demand_pricing: Industry-wide KRA fee cut of ~20% effective 1 April 2026, voluntary and coordinated; KRA base ~INR42-43 crore for FY27.
MF yield compression QoQ under 1%, attributed to passives mix (passives under 10% of AUM); management says no yield cut in individual asset classes. Equity share of AUM ~54-55%.
Mid-sized AMC contract renewals due during FY27; management does not expect material yield decline; a possible 3-5 bps AMC-level pass-through discussed but no concrete RTA fee change agreed.
Licensed domestic AMCs at 31; new AMCs (e.g., Neo, Oaklane) onboarded on scale-play logic. Management says it is selling value rather than price.
IR market share 40%; KRA now number 2 in KRA market after gaining share over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Opex growth of ~10% in FY26 is the lowest in 5 years: how much is deliberate discretionary cost management versus sustainable savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Ram Charan said the cost actions are structural and automation-led, not a one-off squeeze. Headcount rose ~100-120 people YoY, with ReArch hiring offset by a ~70 reduction in core MF operations. Total cost growth was 9% including depreciation and 7.8% excluding it, with QoQ cost growth under 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Passive mix shift typically hurts RTA yields more than AMC yields. Is there scope to renegotiate RTA pricing on passives or to gain bargaining power on the active book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said passives are under 10% of AUM and already priced at very low levels, so there is no room to renegotiate. Yield compression QoQ (<1%) came from mix, not from lower rates in any asset class. Ram Charan said the mix shift is an argument to raise with AMCs, but it is not a decisive one.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 3-5 bps AMC fee cut be passed to RTA fees? Is any RTA fee negotiation under way?
qa_highlights.answer: No concrete RTA fee change has been agreed. Discussions may happen, but management said it is comfortable with the price-value equation and does not expect a material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Should yield decline be modelled at the historical 3-3.5% for FY27 and FY28, given that margins have previously dropped from 46-47% to 42-44%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 3-3.5% is the 5-year average and should be used as a conservative model input, with the aim being a lower number, possibly under 3%. On margins, Anuj Kumar said 46% was reached about 5 quarters ago, dropped to 42%, and has now been regained over 4 quarters. He attributed the earlier fall to investments in non-revenue businesses made over 2022-2025.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 guidance for employee cost, overall expenses and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost growth is guided below 5% and total expense growth below 9%, with increments effective from Q2 FY27. No formal margin guidance was given; the aim is to retain the Q4 FY26 margin of ~46.5% after salary increases, investments and yield compression.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~20% non-MF growth be built in FY27 with KRA flat, and what is the breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a base of ~INR60-62 crore quarterly non-MF revenue, or ~INR250 crore annualised. It needs ~INR45-50 crore of increment: payments ~INR20 crore, AIF ~INR7-8 crore, Rep ~INR7-8 crore, AA/TSP/pension ~INR15 crore (quoted as INR4-5 crore in one place and ~INR15 crore in another), with ConsenPro and GIFT City adding a few crore.

qa_highlights.question: KRA: what is the price cut, and how is FY27 revenue flat after it?
qa_highlights.answer: The industry-wide ~20% fee cut from 1 April 2026 is expected to reduce KRA revenue by ~INR8 crore on a base of ~INR42-43 crore. NSE KRA integration adds ~INR3 crore, leaving a ~INR5 crore gap that management expects to close through new-logo growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is ConsenPro and what is the market opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: ConsenPro is a commercial DPDP-compliance product built inside Think360 from an internal captive offering. It covers consent management, data discovery, regulatory reporting and consulting. Management expects ~40,000-50,000 Indian companies to need it over ~1.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Could a single KYC regime through CKYC reduce KRA pricing or volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CKYC is not yet eligible to substitute for KRA KYC. KRA runs a second verification layer (name match, face match, DOB and address against DigiLocker or UIDAI), so the risk is seen as a watch item rather than an immediate threat.

risks_watch: MF yield: the passive mix shift continues to pull yields down. Any AMC pass-through of 3-5 bps could lead to RTA fee discussions. Management guides yield decline below 3%, against a 3-3.5% historical average, and says no concrete RTA fee change has been agreed.

KRA: a ~INR8 crore fee cut from 1 April 2026 is only partly offset by ~INR3 crore from NSE KRA. FY27 flat guidance depends on new-logo growth to fill a ~INR5 crore gap. A possible single-KYC/CKYC shift is a watch item.

Margin sustainability: management is targeting retention of the ~46.5% Q4 margin through FY27 after salary increases, investments and yield compression. Past cycles show margins falling back to 42-44% after investment phases.

MF AUM and asset growth: AUM fell from INR58.5 lakh crore at a point in Q4 to INR55.1 lakh crore, reflecting Middle East-related market weakness. Management says asset growth is awaited after the last two months, and FY27 MF revenue is not guided.

ReArch execution: a 5-year programme with ~2 years done and ~3-4% behind the schedule curve. The data lake is due in 1H FY27, and the data warehouse and next-gen transaction origination platform are due within 3-4 months. Non-MF margin target is 20% by end FY27.

Non-MF growth dependence: ~20% FY27 growth needs ~INR45-50 crore of incremental revenue. The breakdown includes ~INR20 crore from payments, with a new-logo pipeline (SIFs, ConsenPro, GIFT City) still early.

And I expect that this is kind of a baseline number, which will stick.
We will continue to take these cost actions.
So there is not a onetime squeeze that we have done of everything, and it is not going to be repeatable.
We are taking the maker out completely.
We have a team of close to 200 engineers working on this.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics, cost discipline and non-MF growth, with management calling Q4 a strong quarter. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on FY27 specifics: no formal margin range, no MF growth guidance, and repeated hedging on yields and AMC fee discussions.
